meta.titre: Leakages and Injections: why national income settles where it does
meta.sous_theme: Circular flow, equilibrium conditions in two, three and four sectors

sections.contenu_markdown: When a Cameroonian family saves part of its income, pays tax and buys imported goods, less money returns to local producers as spending. When a foreign buyer purchases Cameroonian cocoa, the government builds a road or a firm buys machines, new spending enters the economy. The balance between these flows decides whether national income rises, falls or stays steady. Papers regularly include questions that ask the student to classify leakages and injections or to state the equilibrium condition in a two, three or four sector economy.

items: Saving is income not spent; taxes are payments to the government; imports are goods and services bought from other countries.
Investment is spending on capital goods, government spending is the purchase of goods and services by the state, and exports are goods and services sold to foreign buyers.
The multiplier is the inverse of the marginal rate of leakage from the circular flow.

sections.titre: Leakages, injections and the equilibrium of national income
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The circular flow
In the circular flow of income, households receive income from firms and spend it on domestic output. Not all income is respent in this way, and not all spending comes from domestic income. **Leakages** (also called withdrawals, $W$) are income not passed on as domestic spending; **injections** ($J$) are spending that does not come from the domestic households' income.

| Leakages ($W$) | Injections ($J$) |
|---|---|
| Saving ($S$) | Investment ($I$) |
| Taxes ($T$) | Government spending on goods and services ($G$) |
| Imports ($M$) | Exports ($X$) |

Transfer payments such as pensions are treated as negative taxes, not as $G$.

### Equilibrium conditions
National income is in equilibrium when planned injections equal planned leakages:

| Economy | Condition |
|---|---|
| Two-sector (households and firms) | $S=I$ |
| Three-sector (adds government) | $S+T=I+G$ |
| Four-sector (adds foreign trade) | $S+T+M=I+G+X$ |

### Adjustment and the multiplier
If $J>W$, spending is above the income that is being passed on, stocks fall, firms raise output and national income rises. If $W>J$, stocks build up and income falls. The size of the change is the multiplier, $k=\frac{1}{\text{marginal leakage rate}}$. A rise in any injection of $\Delta J$ raises income by $k\,\Delta J$.

### Why saving is a leakage even though banks lend
Saving removes money from the spending stream. Banks and other institutions may lend it to firms, which then invest it, but the saver and the investor are different people with different motives, so planned saving can differ from planned investment. Equilibrium is reached only when the two match.

### Sectoral balances
At equilibrium $(S-I)+(T-G)+(M-X)=0$. A private-sector surplus ($S>I$) must be offset by a government deficit ($G>T$) or a trade deficit ($M>X$).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a transaction is described and the student must identify it.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask two questions: is the money withdrawn from the domestic spending stream (leakage) or added to it from outside the households' income (injection)? Then name the category: $S$, $T$ or $M$ for a leakage; $I$, $G$ or $X$ for an injection.

variantes.nom: Calculation question (equilibrium in a four-sector economy)
variantes.quand_utiliser: When functions for $S$, $T$, $M$ and values for $I$, $G$, $X$ are given.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Add all the leakage functions to get one function $W(Y)$, add all the injections to get $J$, set $W=J$ and solve. Check by substituting into every function. The multiplier is $\frac{1}{\text{slope of } W}$.

sections.enonce_markdown:
In a four-sector economy (million FCFA), saving is $S=-40+0.2Y$, taxes are $T=0.1Y$ and imports are $M=20+0.1Y$. Investment is 80, government spending is 100 and exports are 60.

(a) Find equilibrium income.
(b) Show that the leakages and injections balance, and find the budget and trade balances.
(c) Exports rise by 30. Find the multiplier and the new equilibrium income.

etapes.action: Add the leakages into one function.
etapes.justification: All three leakages depend on income and add together.
Equilibrium requires leakages to equal injections.
Compare the leakage and injection of each pair.
The multiplier is the inverse of the slope of the leakage function.
etapes.resultat_markdown: $k=\frac{1}{0.4}=2.5$, so $\Delta Y=2.5\times30=75$ and the new income is 725.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Answers**: (a) $Y=$ **650 million FCFA**; (b) $S+T+M=90+65+85=240$ equals $I+G+X$; the government has a deficit of 35 and the trade balance is a deficit of 25, matched by a private-sector surplus of 10; (c) $k=2.5$ and the new $Y=$ **725 million FCFA**.

items.erreur_markdown: Treating all government spending, including pensions, as an injection.
items.pourquoi_faux: Transfer payments do not buy output directly; they are negative taxes.
items.correction_markdown: Count only government purchases of goods and services as $G$, and treat transfers as negative taxes.

items.erreur_markdown: Classifying imports as an injection because goods come into the country.
items.pourquoi_faux: Money spent on imports goes to foreign producers and leaves the domestic spending stream.
items.correction_markdown: Imports are a leakage; exports are an injection.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing $S=I$ as the equilibrium condition in an economy with government and trade.
Saying that saving is not a leakage because banks lend it to firms.
items.pourquoi_faux: Saving is planned by households and investment by firms, so the two may differ.
items.correction_markdown: Treat saving as a leakage and explain that equilibrium requires planned saving to match the injections.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each item as a leakage or an injection and name the category: (a) a firm buys new machinery from a local supplier; (b) households pay income tax; (c) a wholesaler buys imported rice; (d) foreign buyers purchase Cameroonian coffee; (e) households deposit money in a savings account. Then, if $S=60$, $T=45$, $M=55$, $I=70$ and $G=50$, find the value of $X$ needed for equilibrium.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Injection, investment; (b) leakage, taxes; (c) leakage, imports; (d) injection, exports; (e) leakage, saving. Leakages total $60+45+55=160$; injections without exports are $70+50=120$; so $X=160-120=$ **40**.

items.enonce_markdown: A three-sector economy (million FCFA) has $S=-30+0.2Y$, $T=0.2Y$, $I=50$ and $G=70$. (a) Find equilibrium income and show that leakages equal injections. (b) The government raises spending by 20. Find the new equilibrium income.

A four-sector economy (million FCFA) has $S=-20+0.1Y$, $T=0.1Y$, $M=30+0.2Y$, $I=60$, $G=80$ and $X=110$. (a) Find equilibrium income and the trade balance. (b) Exports fall by 40 because trading partners buy less. Find the new income. (c) Assess whether the government should raise its spending to restore income.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $W=10+0.4Y$ and $J=250$, so $0.4Y=240$ and $Y=$ **600**. Imports are $30+120=150$, so the trade balance is $110-150=$ **$-40$** (deficit). (b) $k=2.5$ and $\Delta Y=-100$, so the new income is **500**; imports fall to 130 and the trade deficit becomes 60. (c) A rise in government spending of 40 would restore the original injections and income, if the multiplier is the same. Arguments in favour: it uses spare resources and is quick to arrange. Arguments against: time lags, rising budget deficit and debt, possible inflation if there is little spare capacity, and extra imports. A judgement should depend on the amount of unemployment and on how the spending is financed.

items_markdown: Leakages are saving, taxes and imports; injections are investment, government spending and exports.
Equilibrium conditions: $S=I$, $S+T=I+G$ and $S+T+M=I+G+X$ for two, three and four sectors.
If injections exceed leakages, income rises; if leakages exceed injections, income falls.
The multiplier is the inverse of the marginal rate of leakage, and a change in an injection is multiplied by it.
